_note: LIVE CONNECTOR + BINDING REGISTRY — the single source for which MCP/analytics/store binding lives on which provider, plus the concrete live IDs (Clarity project ids, analytics login, Shopify stores/themes, Slack channel). Policy prose used to hardcode these and went stale; now prose points here and `bin/connectors.py` renders paste-ready blocks (bot allowlists, ticket templates) from this file. `available_on` is dynamic: when a connector moves seats, edit ONLY this file. This file holds NO secrets — connector NAMES and public IDs only; keys/tokens never live in the repo (see .gitignore, EDGE-CASES §Secrets).
_status_lifecycle: Each mcp_connectors entry carries an OPTIONAL `status`: active | ready | primed. ABSENT = active (every existing connector above is LIVE and unaffected). primed = bundled/declared for distribution but NOT wired; ready = validated + wireable, awaiting owner activation. ONLY active is live-eligible — primed/ready are INERT scaffolding that is never routed, connected, launched, or probed (enforced by bin/routing.connector_is_active + bin/doctor.py check_connector_lifecycle). A primed/ready entry may carry an OPTIONAL `server` block (transport/command/args/url/env_keys/note) that DESCRIBES how it would launch, as DATA only — no script ever executes it. Credentials NEVER live here: `env_keys` names the env vars the admin sets OUT OF BAND at activation; it never holds values. Strap-in mechanism + inert guarantee: mcp-routing.md §MCP strap-in.
_risk_note: CONCENTRATION RISK (known, disclosed): the Shopify and DataForSEO (dfs) integrations ride ONE shared OAuth/KV credential surface — a compromise, token expiry, or outage of that surface can take BOTH down together. Treat them as a single blast radius (one auth-failure / correlated-outage class), not two independent connectors, when routing around an outage (EDGE-CASES.md) or reasoning about secret exposure.

clarity-magnetbaron.note: MCP-judgment seats only, and only dashboard + a handful of flagged recordings. Bulk recording pulls (up to 250 rows) are a banned row-dump — park volume; Heat Map bot handles browser-only layers.

mb-bundled-example.note: PRIMED distribution scaffold — bundled as DATA so a distributed clone carries this MCP plug-and-play, but it is NOT wired. INERT: primed/ready is never routed, connected, launched, or probed; `available_on` here DECLARES the seat this MCP would ride on once activated, and the router still refuses to grant it while status != active (proven by bin/routing.connector_is_active + bin/doctor.py check_connector_lifecycle + bin/smoketest.py). The admin lifts it primed→ready→active out of band; only then is it live.

server.note: Launch DESCRIPTOR carried as data only — no process is spawned and no socket opened from this block. Credentials never live in-repo: `env_keys` NAMES the env var(s) the admin sets out of band at activation; values never appear here.
